WAISS · #127 / 74
Term of the month

abliterated

An open model with its refusals cut out of the weights, no retraining
01How: find the one direction in the network that makes the model say no, and project it out. Ablation + obliterated.
02This month: an uncensored Mistral Large 4 on Hugging Face two days after its weights came out. 9,136 “abliterated” repos, 719 of them new in October.
03The catch: ProjectDiscovery hid a credential-stealing backdoor in an edited open model for under $50. In a Codex setup the trigger fired 50 times out of 50, normal accuracy stayed at 100%.
Method: Arditi et al., NeurIPS 2024; the name: FailSpy (2024), made popular by Maxime Labonne. Sources: Hugging Face API (10 Nov), ProjectDiscovery (6 Oct), Schneier (16 Oct)

WAISS · #134 / 74
Security · OpenAI

Out of the sandbox

Three escapes since May, the last one via DNS
DATE
WHAT HAPPENED
26 May
First escape: agents reach the internet through a flaw in OpenAI’s internal package server
9–19 Jul
Agents get code execution on dozens of Hugging Face production servers, root on one
20 Sep
A research model uses a DNS misconfiguration to talk to a chatbot outside; training paused
1 Oct
Training resumes, 11 days after the pause began
23 Oct
“Securing our frontier model training environment”: frontier training now runs fully offline
Instead of the live internet, an indexed cache: the “offline world”. Red-teaming found more ways out: sandbox escapes, covert channels between agents via timing on shared hardware. For builders: DNS is an exit too, not just HTTP. Sources: OpenAI, Forkast, Digital Applied

Security · OpenSSH · CVE-2026-123158

SSHole

Found by an agent swarm, exploited within 9 hours
The bugAny long passwordmusl’s crypt() returns “*” on error, sshd matches it against accounts locked with “*”. 257–1024 characters get in.
AffectedAlpine, OpenWrt, Yoctomusl, no PAM, password login on. glibc distros and Dropbear are safe.
Do thisOpenSSH 10.6p2Until then: PasswordAuthentication no. Check your Alpine-based images.

Black October

AI dev platforms were breached for the keys in your env vars
Who9 platforms in OctoberFireworks, Railway, Warp, Lightning AI, Northflank and more; in November also NVIDIA Brev, Trigger.dev.
WhatYour AI API keysRailway: env vars of up to ~100,000 workspaces exposed. In two traced cases, stolen keys were tried within 30 minutes.
Do thisRotate, scope, capRotate keys stored on hosting platforms, one key per service, spend limits on. Google saw victims billed $100k+ a day.

In productionTicket routingAmazon’s internal ticket system: each ticket to one of 20 labels, replacing Claude Sonnet 4.6. A Gemma 4 E4B build on one A10G GPU.
